name: Autocratic monarchy
what: One hereditary ruler holds supreme power with no body that can legally overrule them.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Monarchy sharing power
what: A monarch rules, but nobles, electors or estates hold power the crown has to bargain with.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Constitutional monarchy
what: A monarch whose powers are limited by a written or customary constitution and an elected parliament.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Monarchy (kind not recorded)
what: A hereditary or elective monarchy; the source does not say how far the ruler was limited.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Religious rule
what: Rulers whose authority rests on a religious office: caliphs, imams, popes, god-kings.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Republic of the few
what: No monarch; magistrates are chosen by and from a narrow class of nobles, merchants or citizens.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Republic (kind not recorded)
what: No monarch; the source does not say how many people could vote.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Democracy
what: Rulers are chosen in contested elections by a broad body of citizens.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: One-party state
what: A single party monopolises power and elections offer no real choice.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Dictatorship
what: A general, junta or strongman rules without hereditary claim or real elections.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Ruled from abroad
what: A colony, protectorate or puppet whose real government sits in another state.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Tribal or steppe confederation
what: Clans or tribes bound by a leader chosen among chiefs, often by acclaim or council (kurultai).

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Absolute monarchy
what: The monarch makes law, commands the army and appoints all officials; no assembly can veto them.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Divine kingship
what: The ruler is himself treated as a god or the living link to the gods, so obeying him is a religious duty.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Bureaucratic monarchy
what: An emperor or king rules through a salaried, ranked civil service rather than through landed nobles.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

example: Han and Tang China, Joseon Korea

name: Principate
what: One man holds supreme power while keeping the outward forms of a republic: senate, consuls, elections.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Dominate
what: An openly autocratic emperor, addressed as lord (dominus), with the republican forms dropped.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Feudal monarchy
what: The king grants land to nobles in return for military service; real power is spread among those vassals.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Elective monarchy
what: The monarch is chosen by an electoral body (nobles, princes, electors) rather than by birth alone.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Shogunate (military feudal rule)
what: A hereditary military ruler governs in the name of a powerless sovereign, through sworn vassal lords.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Constitutional monarchy
what: A written constitution limits the monarch, who still appoints and leads the government.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Parliamentary monarchy
what: The monarch reigns but the government answers to an elected parliament.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Monarchy
what: Rule by a king, queen, emperor, sultan or prince.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Caliphate
what: The caliph rules as successor to the Prophet Muhammad, head of the Muslim community in politics and faith.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Theocracy
what: Clergy or a religious leader hold supreme political authority.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

example: Papal States, Islamic Republic of Iran

name: Aristocratic republic
what: Elected magistrates and councils, but only a hereditary or wealthy elite can hold office or vote.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Racially exclusive democracy
what: Elections are real for one racial group while the majority is barred from voting.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Republic
what: A state without a monarch, headed by elected or appointed officials.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Parliamentary republic
what: The government answers to parliament; the head of state is a separate, often ceremonial president.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Presidential republic
what: An elected president is both head of state and head of government, separate from the legislature.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Direct democracy
what: Citizens vote on laws themselves in an assembly, and most offices are filled by lot.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Representative democracy
what: Citizens elect representatives in free, contested elections with broad suffrage.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: One-party state
what: One party controls the state and elections; rivals are banned.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

example: Soviet Union, People's Republic of China

name: Fascist one-party state
what: A single nationalist party led by a leader with unlimited power, mass mobilisation and terror.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Military dictatorship
what: The armed forces or a junta of officers govern directly.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Personal dictatorship
what: A single strongman rules through loyalists, outside any party or dynasty.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Colony
what: Governed directly by officials sent from a foreign metropole.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Protectorate or vassal
what: Keeps its own ruler but a stronger state controls its foreign policy and often more.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Puppet state
what: Nominally independent, in fact run by an occupying power.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Steppe khaganate
what: A confederation of nomadic tribes under a khan or khagan, confirmed by a council of chiefs (kurultai).

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Chiefdom or tribal confederation
what: Ranked clans under paramount chiefs, without a permanent bureaucracy.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: List of forms of government

name: Written law codes
what: Laws written down and published so judges and subjects can know them.
why: A written code binds rulers and judges to stated rules and makes law outlive the lawgiver.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Written law codes

name: Limits on rulers
what: Charters and constitutions that bind the ruler to law and give a council or parliament a say.
why: Whether power is bounded decides whether rights survive a bad ruler.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Constitutionalism

name: Civil service by examination
what: Officials chosen by written examination rather than birth or patronage.
why: Merit selection let empires recruit talent outside the aristocracy and bound elites to the state.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Civil service by examination

name: Slave trade
what: Buying, selling and shipping enslaved people across borders.
why: Banning the trade came before banning slavery itself almost everywhere; the two are separate steps.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Slave trade

name: Slavery
what: People held as property who can be bought, sold and inherited.
why: Slavery was legal in most states in history; its abolition is one of the sharpest breaks in human institutions.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Slavery

name: Serfdom
what: Peasants legally bound to the land and owing labour or dues to a lord, but not sold as chattel.
why: Serfdom shaped who could move, marry, own land or join armies across Europe and beyond.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Serfdom

name: Religious toleration
what: The state lets people of other faiths worship, or stops forcing one faith.
why: Toleration edicts and their revocation explain migrations, revolts and where minorities survived.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Religious toleration

name: Votes for all men
what: Every adult man may vote, without a property, tax or race test.
why: Mass male suffrage turned elections into contests for the whole population.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Votes for all men

name: Votes for women
what: Women may vote on the same terms as men.
why: Before women could vote, half the adult population had no say in any electoral system.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Votes for women

name: Legal racial segregation
what: Laws that separate people by race in voting, schooling, marriage or residence.
why: Segregation regimes kept racial hierarchy alive after slavery ended.

sources.cite: Wikipedia: Legal racial segregation
